records.purpose: Professional and facility directories share the existing account/practitioner/organization owner; they do not create a new clinical truth store or an owner per specialty. Preserve qualifications, expertise, biography/publications, languages, international certification and network affiliations; verify source, issuing authority, scope, expiry and status. Retain center-specific dialysis, endoscopy, transfusion, infusion, isolation/ICU, laser, rehabilitation, surgery, diagnostic, maternity/delivery and working-hour/contact capabilities. A directory claim is not current staffing, treatment privilege or patient-data authorization. Fertility success rates require denominator/time/cohort provenance and must not be treated as a personal outcome estimate.
records.scope: Append-only providers profile; no replacement of earlier owner profiles
records.workflow: Capture attributed practitioner/organization claim → verify credential and role scope/expiry separately → retain specialty and facility capability profiles → publish purpose-limited directory projection → correct/version with provenance. Clinical record access requires a separate current authorization decision.
records.clinical_safety: No credential, directory membership, risk score or clinical model can grant treatment authority or unrestricted patient access. Fail closed for the non-emergency MVP read; do not claim emergency response, clinical clearance or certification.
records.privacy: Purpose-limited minimum disclosure with separate tenant/patient/recipient checks, guardian/adolescent restrictions and protected credential/audit metadata. No raw bearer tokens, biometric samples or unrestricted health payloads in logs.
records.failure_modes: Unknown, expired, revoked, contradictory or unavailable identity/role/grant/source yields denial or explicit unavailable state. Preserve source history and idempotent correction; never silently expand permissions on retry.
records.acceptance: Trace every nonempty source fragment to a canonical anchor; verify credential and facility differences survive normalization. Future runtime acceptance must cover wrong patient/tenant/purpose, revoked/expired role, dependency failure, stale source and concurrent revoke/read. Structural tests do not establish runtime protection.
records.open_gates: Typed schemas, current policy/provider configuration, runtime and qualified acceptance evidence are incomplete.

Retain center-specific dialysis, endoscopy, transfusion, infusion, isolation/ICU, laser, rehabilitation, surgery, diagnostic, maternity/delivery and working-hour/contact capabilities. A directory claim is not current staffing, treatment privilege or patient-data authorization. Fertility success rates require denominator/time/cohort provenance and must not be treated as a personal outcome estimate.
records.scope: Append-only providers profile; no replacement of earlier owner profiles
records.workflow: Capture attributed practitioner/organization claim → verify credential and role scope/expiry separately → retain specialty and facility capability profiles → publish purpose-limited directory projection → correct/version with provenance. Clinical record access requires a separate current authorization decision.
records.clinical_safety: No credential, directory membership, risk score or clinical model can grant treatment authority or unrestricted patient access. Fail closed for the non-emergency MVP read; do not claim emergency response, clinical clearance or certification.
records.privacy: Purpose-limited minimum disclosure with separate tenant/patient/recipient checks, guardian/adolescent restrictions and protected credential/audit metadata. No raw bearer tokens, biometric samples or unrestricted health payloads in logs.
records.failure_modes: Unknown, expired, revoked, contradictory or unavailable identity/role/grant/source yields denial or explicit unavailable state. Preserve source history and idempotent correction; never silently expand permissions on retry.
records.acceptance: Trace every nonempty source fragment to a canonical anchor; verify credential and facility differences survive normalization. Future runtime acceptance must cover wrong patient/tenant/purpose, revoked/expired role, dependency failure, stale source and concurrent revoke/read. Structural tests do not establish runtime protection.
records.open_gates: Typed schemas, current policy/provider configuration, runtime and qualified acceptance evidence are incomplete.

Structural tests do not establish runtime protection.

records.purpose: Security architecture, per-request zero-trust enforcement and monitoring form one existing shared security owner. Identity supplies authenticated subject/session; Consent supplies policy/grant and legal-authority evidence; Security enforces action/resource/context and Audit records outcomes. Authentication alone never authorizes patient data. Legacy ABAC marked future cannot defer patient/purpose/recipient checks required by the current MVP. Preserve mobile/server/API/encryption/monitoring and future HSM/confidential/quantum-resistant intentions without claiming certification or implementation.
records.scope: Append-only security profile; no replacement of earlier owner profiles
records.workflow: Authenticate trusted context via identity → resolve current role, patient binding, resource/version, purpose and grant/policy → enforce default-deny → acquire durable audit acknowledgement → release only authorized projection. Reject missing/stale/ambiguous attributes and dependency failures; monitoring anomalies require qualified review rather than automatic clinical access escalation.
